title: Window-loop machine construction
statement: Given a natural number $K$, types $Q,T,P_t,P_s$, Turing machines $R_t$ with one work tape and $R_s$ with $K+1$ work tapes, and states $t_e,t_y,t_n\in P_t$ and $s_e,s_y,s_n\in P_s$, assume that equality is decidable on $P_t$ and $P_s$. The definition constructs a Turing machine with $K+1$ work tapes over the record alphabet and control states in the dependent sum of the four phases (anchor, test, step, and stop); its initial control is the anchor phase with unit value, and its transitions use the phase-specific machines and phase changes determined by the given states.
hypotheses_covered: Machine $R_t$ with one work tape over the record alphabet
Machine $R_s$ with $K+1$ work tapes over the record alphabet
caveat: The supplied statement refers to the phase-row construction and phase-redirection function without including their definitions, so their precise transition behavior cannot be specified from the payload.
